title: ECSS-E-ST-40C Rev.1, Space engineering: Software
body: The engineering standard the package follows: the requirements baseline (5.2), the technical specification (5.4), the design (5.5), the validation (5.6), the delivery and acceptance (5.7), the verification (5.8) and the DRDs of its annexes. Cited, never copied.
rationale: The documents' structure and the reviews' contents.

title: ECSS-Q-ST-80C Rev.2, Space product assurance: Software product assurance
body: The product assurance standard: the software criticality categories (6.2.2) the tailoring argues from. Cited, never copied.
rationale: The category and its consequences on the activities.

title: ISO/IEC 9899:2011, 7.17 Atomics
body: The C11 memory model: atomic objects, memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_acquire and memory_order_release, atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit and its spurious failures, the synchronizes-with relation, atomic_is_lock_free and the ATOMIC_*_LOCK_FREE macros.
rationale: The words in which the ordering requirements are stated and inspected.

title: Vyukov, Bounded MPMC queue
body: D. Vyukov, Bounded MPMC queue, 1024cores.net (https://www.1024cores.net/home/lock-free-algorithms/queues/bounded-mpmc-queue): the per-slot sequence, the claim by compare-and-swap on one shared position, and the author's own note that a producer stalled between claim and publish blocks the consumer, so the queue is not formally lock-free.
rationale: The algorithm MPSCring implements, restricted to one consumer.

title: Herlihy, Wait-free synchronization (1991)
body: M. Herlihy, Wait-free synchronization, ACM Transactions on Programming Languages and Systems 13(1), 1991: wait-freedom and lock-freedom, the progress conditions SRS-012 and SRS-013 use.

title: The repository's README at 1.0.10
body: README.md of MPSCring at 73bb6fe3: the API contract, the implementation choices, the lock-free target support, the build system, the profiles and hardening.
rationale: The supplier's own statement of its contract, read against the header and the code.

title: kyr_core 5.0.0, the customer's use
body: kyr_core at aa7479c8 (v5.0.0): the write queue, one ring of 1024 per environment, any request thread submitting a job within a 250 ms admission budget, the environment's one writer taking batches of 32 and sleeping on its condition while the ring is empty, the stop joining the writer and draining from the stopping thread; every module's durable write goes through it (kyr_drive, kyr_estate, kyr_rms).
rationale: Where the requirements baseline comes from: the customer's code.
